# Satellite Briefing — Style Prompt

> Real satellite imagery of a real place, graded down to an analyst's grey, with thin white measurement lines drawn on the ground: a lock-on reticle, outlines, a range line, one reading. One continuous zoom built from stacked imagery plates carries the viewer from orbit to the ground and back, and time can run inside one locked frame.
> References (grammar only): open-source investigation films that annotate satellite pictures (thin lines on imagery, one claim per screen, measuring as the plot); the Eameses' *Powers of Ten* (one continuous change of scale with a readout); NASA Earth Observatory's *World of Change* (one place, time running). Copy none of their layouts, typefaces, icons or music; never name them in the film.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- **The ground is a photograph**: real, licence-clean, georeferenced satellite or aerial imagery of the actual place. Nothing on the ground is drawn, stylised or generated.
- **Two layers, two truths**: the imagery is what the satellite saw; the hairlines are what the analyst measured. Marks are thin, white, sparse, and sit on real coordinates.
- **The grade moves with the story**: orbit in true colour, the analysis layer in grey, colour back only where the story turns.
- **Scale is the camera**: one zoom from orbit to the ground built from nested plates, with an altitude readout and a scale bar from the same camera.
- **One finding per screen**, in the single accent colour.

Not Data Storytelling (a chart on paper), not Sci-fi Hologram HUD (no glowing wireframes or invented chrome), not Blueprint, not Isometric Infographic (real nadir or oblique views, no diorama), not a keynote (no slides, header bars or chapter numbers).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Plates**: georeferenced rasters with a lon/lat box, sampled in a shader where the camera ray hits the ground, nested by resolution (world → region → detail) with feathered edges so finer plates dissolve in as the camera descends.
- **Globe**: ray–sphere from a perspective camera, a thin atmosphere rim, limb shading at orbit only; compute |C|² − R² in double precision (float32 fails below a few tens of km).
- **Time**: dated plates share one grid. A soft scan front (a satellite pass, never a hairline) swaps them: north → south forward, south → north for a rewind. Growth can run outward from the old edge, ordered by a distance map.
- **The analyst's grade** (one uniform from colour to grey): luminance with local contrast and clarity, a shoulder so salt, snow and cloud stay below white, toned blue-black → cool silver up to ~65 % grey, a fifth of the chroma. White belongs to the marks.
- **Marks**: a 2D overlay through the same world → screen function: hairlines 1.2–2.6 px with a dark halo, dashes for history and claims, brackets, ticks, leader lines. Lines draw on; outlines print behind the scan.
- **Screen space only for instruments** (altitude, scale bar, imagery credit) and the transcript strip. Everything else is anchored to the ground.
- **The claim layer** is a printed map drawn in the shader from a distance field of the old outline: paper grain a few pixels wide at any zoom, halftone ink, coast and waterlines, graticule, the serif name.
- **Post**: light grain in ffmpeg, a vignette, directional blur only on whip pans.

## 3. Colour logic

- Neutral ground: grey, roughly 3–65 % in value. White means *measured*.
- One accent (warm, e.g. amber) for the single reading on screen, never decoration.
- A second hue may mark the **claim** the imagery tests (a map, a plan, a promise): flat, cartographic, never used for anything measured.
- True colour is evidence: at orbit, and again only where the story turns (the field that greened, the water that returned).
- No false-colour ramps over the imagery.

Example (our demo): ground #070B0E → #A1A7A9, marks #F2F5F6, reading #FFBE55, map blue rgb(46, 112, 206).

## 4. Type & subtitles

- **Roles**: a light condensed grotesk for the reading (96–130 px, e.g. Barlow Condensed); a monospace for instruments and dates (20–34 px, e.g. IBM Plex Mono); a sans for labels in the film's language (24–42 px); a serif only for the claim layer and the title. OFL, self-hosted, CJK subset to the characters used.
- **Labels attach to the ground** with a leader line. The reading sits in the right third beside what it measures, label above, source note below ("Landsat, measured").
- **Subtitles are a transcript strip** at the bottom left: a 2 px white rule, a dark plate fading right, left-aligned, each line on one line (measure with the real font, `nowrap`; split a long sentence into two cues). If the film is bilingual, the film's language on top.
- Nothing below 20 px at 1080p, the imagery credit included.
- Hold subtitles ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s); a rolling counter reports its landing value; labels stay ≥ characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5 s (CJK).

## 5. Motion quality

- The camera never stops: distance interpolates in log space, segments ease, holds keep a 2–5 % creep or a slow rotation. No frozen frame longer than a second.
- Marks arrive by being made: a line grows, an outline prints behind the scan, a counter rolls and lands with a small pop, a reticle snaps with overshoot.
- Time changes are scans, never dissolves; their spacing tells the speed, and the camera moves with them (accelerating as the steps shorten, braking on the last).
- Never moves: the ground under its annotations, the instrument positions.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Oblique orbit, limb in frame | scale, context, distance | an opening; a return; a title card |
| Dive (log zoom, tilt to nadir) | going to look for yourself | a reveal; checking a claim |
| Locked nadir frame, slow creep | evidence, comparison | time running in one place; a measurement |
| Push-in on a point | singling out | one town, one dam, one field |
| Track along a line | travelling a distance | measuring; a river, a road, a border |
| Whip pan with blur | a new subject at the same altitude | the counter-example; "meanwhile" |
| Climb back to orbit | consequence, perspective | an ending; a summary |

At key moments the subject fills a third of the frame height; reading right, subtitles bottom left, instruments in the corners. Transitions: scan-line swaps, a map layer switched off, zooming through plates, whip pans, the reticle opening into a title card. No crossfades between unrelated places, no hard cuts inside a zoom.

## 7. Sound palette

- **Telemetry**: FM pings (a lock-on ping worth bringing back), dry ticks on the grid that divide to accelerate, noise scans (rising for a rewind, falling forward), servo whines, a ratchet for a range line.
- **Weight**: timpani, bass drum, gran cassa, bowed cymbal, a tam-tam reversed when time runs backwards. Measurements land on a pitched hit.
- **Synthesis**: a pulse bass with audible 2nd and 3rd harmonics, detuned-saw pads under a low-pass, risers for dives.
- **Beds**: orbit hum, radio hiss, data chatter; the place's own ambience (wind, water, a far horn), sparingly, often as J- or L-cuts.
- **One option for the shape**: keep the palette dry (electronics, skins, metal) and let one wet timbre (glass, water, bowed metal) mark the turn.
- **Silence**: music and foley stop, a thin bed stays, impacts may decay into it; the first sound after it is the turn. A short suck-out (0.2–0.45 s, music and foley down ~25 dB) before the heaviest impacts makes them land.
- **Mix**: voice ~10 dB over music; the two or three designed impacts are the loudest moments (out of the bus compressor, with mid-range body, e.g. a low-brass stab); 20–60 Hz about 15 dB under the full band (high-pass ~40 Hz, impact weight at 60–120 Hz); −14 LUFS, true peak ≤ −1.2 dB. Voice: a calm analyst, short declarative lines.

## 8. Native moves

- **The map against the photograph.** The camera falls into the printed map of the claim; a scanner bar tears it away and the ground is underneath; the name outlives the page. *Fits content like:* a lake still on maps but gone; a cleared concession forest; a planned city never built.
- **Time rings in a locked frame.** Dated plates scan in one by one; each leaves its outline, the band lost between two rings flashes. *Fits content like:* a glacier's retreat; a city's sprawl; a fire scar season after season.
- **The range line.** Mark the destination, grow a ticked line from A to B, chase the tip while the reading counts up, land on the number, pull back to show the whole distance. *Fits content like:* how far a shore moved; a village to its well; a camp to the border.
- **The dive and the climb.** One zoom from orbit to the ground, or back. *Fits content like:* locating anything; a scale reveal; an ending that returns one place to the planet.
- **Colour returns where the story turns.** Only the subject regains true colour inside the grey. *Fits content like:* an irrigated field; a refilled reservoir; a regrown forest.
- **The reticle becomes the frame**: the lock-on brackets open out to frame a title card or the last reading.

## 9. Pitfalls of the medium

- **Licences**: not usable: Google Earth/Maps, Bing, Esri World Imagery, Mapbox Satellite, Planet, Maxar, news photos, AI-generated imagery. EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless is CC BY 4.0 only for 2016 (2018 onward is NC). Raw Copernicus Sentinel data need "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [year]"; check the user's rules. Public domain or free with credit: USGS Landsat (1972 on, worldwide), USGS NAIP (US, ~1 m), NASA Blue Marble, MODIS, VIIRS. Burn a readable credit into the picture and list every asset in `CREDITS`.
- **Finding imagery for a new place**: search by bounding box and date in the Planetary Computer STAC (Landsat C2, Sentinel-2 L2A; no account) or USGS EarthExplorer; MODIS/VIIRS and Blue Marble from NASA GIBS; outlines from Natural Earth. Log every request. OSM (ODbL), CC BY-SA and "no known restrictions" are not CC0: name the terms and ask the user first. Ask for the user's own surveys or GIS layers when the place is theirs. Never fill a gap with generated imagery presented as evidence.
- **Seams**: paths imaged on other days disagree. One date per path, each scene gain-matched on stable land, feathered overlaps, holes filled from the same year only.
- **Old sensors**: Landsat MSS (to 1992) has no blue or SWIR and drops scan lines: nearest-neighbour resampling, near-zero rows as nodata filled from same-year scenes, scan-angle streaks cleaned on land only. Inspect every year at full contrast.
- **Plumes and haze** cross water as bright diagonal bands: swap the scene for another date of the same year rather than painting it out.
- **Edges**: resampling against nodata darkens scene rims (erode the mask); drop contour pieces along a plate border. Real straight edges (dikes, polders) can read as seams: frame them out or label them.
- **Grey mush at close range**: raise local contrast for that altitude only and dim outside the measured corridor.
- **Water and cloud**: MNDWI where shortwave infrared exists, only the basin you measure; clouds read as features in grey, so use the dry season.
- **Facts**: keep a FACTS.md in the project folder (claim, source URL, quoted wording, or the measurement method with scene IDs and dates) and deliver it with the film. Measure on the date you show.

## 10. Engine

- `demo/engine.js`: `makeCamera({lat, lon, d, tilt, heading, sx, sy})`, `project()` / `unproject()`, the WebGL2 plate shader (nested plates, time scans, growth map, analyst grade, printed-map layer, whip blur).
- `demo/overlay.js`: hairlines, brackets, `readout`, the measured single-line `subtitle` strip, `text` with a registry for `window.TEXTS`.
- `demo/tools/`: `fetch_landsat.py` (STAC, one date per path, same-year gap fill), `plates.py` (normalisation, streak cleaning, water masks, areas), `vectors.py` (shorelines, distances), `mapfield.py` (the printed map), `growth.py`.
- **Extra packages and packs**: none beyond `setup.sh deps voice` and the sample packs the score uses (`sh tools/fetch.sh instruments <lib>` for vsco2ce, vcsl, freepats in the demo). Imagery uses only the standard library, numpy, SciPy, Pillow (no GDAL); allow 3–4 GB for cached scenes. Anything more (rasterio, pyproj) goes in a private venv in the project folder, not `$LIB/.venv`.

## 11. Variation space

The agent decides the place or places, whether there is a claim layer, which dates, the structure, the camera path, the accent hue and where colour comes back.

- **Structures**: a locked time-lapse of one place ending in a push-in; a river followed from source to mouth with a reading at each stop; two places compared at one scale with whip pans.
- **Openings**: a ground-level detail that climbs to reveal its scale; a black frame a scan line paints in; an oblique orbit with a searching reticle.
- **Endings**: the climb back to orbit; a last measurement that lands and holds in silence; the claim layer redrawn to match the ground.

---

How our demo was made (story, shots, score, end card, build): [DEMO.md](DEMO.md). Read it after your treatment exists.

# Satellite Briefing — our demo

Demo: *The Map Still Says Sea* 《地图上还写着海》 (37.8 s) · `satellite-briefing.mp4` · source in [`demo/`](demo/)

A satellite follows the map to a sea and finds a desert; the only part that came back is the part someone dammed. The Aral Sea, 1977–2025, on public-domain Landsat imagery. Chinese on screen, English narration, bilingual subtitles (Chinese line above, English line below).

## Story & structure

Logline: on the map it is still the Aral Sea; from orbit it is salt and sand; the one piece of it that returned, the North Aral, was kept by a 13 km dike.

Arc: a claim (a printed atlas page of the 1960 sea, its serif name 咸海) → the check (a dive into the map until it fills the frame, a scanner bar tears it away: salt crust, then silence) → the evidence (time rewound to 1977 and played forward in one locked frame, each year leaving its shoreline as a ring, the rings coming faster and faster) → the human scale (a range line from Muynak's old harbour to today's sea, 95 km) → the turn (silence, then water heard before it is seen, a whip pan north to the Kok-Aral dike, rings that grow outward, the water's true colour coming back) → the ending (the label 咸海 leaves the empty basin and pins itself to the North Aral; back to orbit).

Native moves spent: *the map against the photograph* at the reveal; *time rings in a locked frame* as the signature shot; *the range line* for the human scale; *colour returns where the story turns* for the North Aral; *the dive and the climb* as bookends; *the reticle becomes the frame* for the end card.

Measured values are labelled as measured on screen; every number and its source is in [`demo/FACTS.md`](demo/FACTS.md).

## Shots

One continuous take; framing changes by altitude. Times in seconds.

| # | Time | Shot | Camera | Native move / note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0–1.8 | Earth's limb across the top, Central Asia below; a reticle searching, locks at 0.6; map layer on at 1.2 | oblique orbit (tilt 57°), lateral drift from frame 0 | the lock ping is the film's key sound |
| 2 | 1.8–5.4 | the sea's blue becomes a whole printed page as we fall into it: paper grain, a halftone in the ink, a fold, waterlines along the east coast, graticule, Amu Darya and Syr Darya, town dots, the serif name growing to the frame centre | dive, 3,800 → 160 km, tilt 55° → 0°, accelerate then brake; the coast stays in frame | the ground beneath drains to grey |
| 3 | 5.36–6.6 | a scanner bar sweeps down the frame and tears the page away (0.34 s): wind-streaked salt crust underneath, 咸海 left floating over it | settle 160 → 46 km | a 0.45 s suck-out before the tear; silence 1 from ~5.9 |
| 4 | 6.6–7.8 | five upward scans 2025 → 2014 → 2009 → 2000 → 1989 → 1977, a year counter steps back | climb 29 → 900 km, ease-out | first sound after silence: the rewind |
| 5 | 7.8–13.2 | **signature**: the whole sea, everything outside the old shore dimmed; six soft downward scans each print a shoreline ring (1977, 1989, 2000, 2009, 2014, 2025) at 1.8 / 1.2 / 0.9 / 0.6 / 0.9 s spacing; the lost band flashes; a light runs along the newest shore; reading 80 % → 7 % (dimmed while it rolls, bright when it lands) | nadir orbit: 980 → 600 km and 0° → −15° rotation on an accelerating curve (motion per second 1.2 → 3.9), braking in 0.3 s on the stop | the camera speeds up with the rings and stops with them |

| 7 | 15.3–17.4 | the reticle holds the port through the push, the rest dimmed; 16.2 the port label with the ship horn; 16.5 the 1977 shoreline (measured) is drawn past the port, "1977 年岸线", the water lost since 1977 a faint wash | pure push on the port, 520 → 92 km, port at the centre | lands readable: the port at the old water's edge |

| 10 | 24.0–28.8 | Kok-Aral dike traced (24.0–24.6, slam on "dam"); 2001 ring at 25.2; the 2009 water grows outward from the 2001 shore (25.3–26.4) and the 2009 ring stamps where it stops; only the North Aral's water regains true colour; a light runs along the new shore; reading +37 % | push 44 → 24 km with a 7° turn | water growing outward = the turn |
| 11 | 28.8–34.2 | north plate becomes 2025 under the climb; the label 咸海 slides from the empty basin and pins to the North Aral (30.6–31.2); colour returns everywhere | climb to orbit, tilt back to 50° | L-cut: the water fades under the climb |
| 12 | 34.2–37.8 | the lock brackets open into the end-card frame; one last satellite pass sweeps behind the title | Earth turns under a dimmed oblique orbit | end card |

## Score structure

100 BPM, 4/4; every key action on a beat or half-beat (`demo/tools/cuecheck.py`: 0 ms on 26 cues). D minor, turning to D major at the dam.

| Section | Time | Palette | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orbit | 0–1.8 | D drone (pulse bass with 2nd/3rd harmonics), Dm pad, FM telemetry plucks in 8ths, orbit hum, radio hiss, data chatter | lock ping D6 at 0.6, map ping A5 at 1.2 |
| Dive | 1.8–4.95 | plucks to 16ths with the filter opening, hi-hat ticks, noise riser, gran cassa crescendo, rising tone, altitude-counter clicks | everything is sucked out 4.95–5.36 |
| Tear | 5.4 | the map torn away: bass drum, gran cassa, timpani, a fortissimo low-brass stab (trombones, tuba, horns, D minor), crash, a crackling paper rip swept with the scan bar | one of the three heaviest moments |
| Silence 1 | ~5.9–6.6 | thin wind; the tear decays into it | |
| Rewind | 6.6–7.8 | the last 1.8 s of the film's own soundtrack played backwards and speeding up, a reversed tam-tam, counter ticks | the turn into the signature shot |
| Rings | 7.8–13.2 | bass descends D–C–B♭–A–G with the chords Dm–C–B♭–A–Gm (two pad layers); tuba on each root, trombone on the fifth; a sub pulse on every beat, every half beat from 2000; ticks 8ths → 16ths; each ring: timpani on the root + bass drum + inharmonic metal ring + pen hiss; a reversed cymbal swells into a 0.24 s suck-out | acceleration by subdivision, not tempo |
| Stop | 13.2–15.3 | the slam (bass drum, timpani, gran cassa, gong, metal clang), then low D, bowed cymbal, thin drone | the loudest moment of the film |
| Muynak | 15.3–21.9 | distant ship horn (two detuned saws, long room) with a creak, timpani heartbeat every two beats, a low D/A drone whose filter opens with the range line, dry sand grains, ratchet ticks per 2 km (accent every 10 km), a hollow tock + ping when the reading lands | |
| Silence 2 | 21.9–22.8 | wind only | first sound after it: one lap of water at 22.8, before the picture turns north |
| North | 22.8–28.8 | whip crack and swish; a 0.22 s suck-out, then the dam slam (bass drum, timpani, knock, clash, low metal gate); D major: tuba, trombone, horns, a warm pad, bowed vibraphone, a cymbal swell that lands as the water arrives, glass-harp motif D5–A4–C♯5–F♯5–E5–D5 with echoes, vibraphone pulse; water bed | the only wet timbres in the film |
| Climb | 28.8–34.2 | horns D3/A3/F♯4, tuba, bowed vibraphone, D-major pad; the motif on glass and FM ping together (dry and wet united); light pulse | pin ping at 31.2 |
| End | 34.2–37.8 | low D hit, lock-ping echo, a soft sweep for the last pass, long tail | |

Mix (in `mix.py`): stem gains frozen (music 10 dB under the voice while it speaks and ducked about 5 dB, pulse −8 dB, foley −6 dB, beds −17 dB); bus compression on music, pulse, foley and beds only, so the hits keep their weight; a master stage (−14.4 LUFS, true-peak limiter at −4.6 dBTP on 4× oversampled peaks; AAC adds back about 3 dB). Sub-bass: a 38 Hz high-pass (46 Hz, 4th order on hits) and a −5 dB shelf below 62 Hz on everything but the voice; the impacts carry their weight at 60–120 Hz (`punch()`): 20–60 Hz sits 16 dB under the full band, as in the dataviz demo. The film measures −13.8 LUFS, true peak −1.6 dBTP, LRA 5.3 LU. `tools/impactcheck.py`: the hard stop is the loudest momentary moment of the film, the dam slam −0.5 dB and the map tear −2.6 dB under it (each among the loudest 4 s of the film), and they follow dips of −4, −3 and −14 dB. Silences sit about 20 dB under the program.

## Palette & props

- Ground: Landsat true colour at orbit; the analysis grade from #070B0E to #A1A7A9 with a fifth of the chroma.
- Marks #F2F5F6 with dark halos; the reading amber #FFBE55; the printed map: paper #ECE2CB, sea #8CB5DB, coast ink #1A3B6B, graticule in a faded red-brown, the serif name in #1F3F6B on the page and #D6EAFF over the sand.
- The North Aral water returns to a lifted true colour inside a 0.75° circle; nothing else in the analysis layer is coloured.
- Props: the printed map (Natural Earth historic-lake polygon as a distance field, rivers, two town dots), six measured shorelines (1977–2025), the North Aral rings (2001, 2009), the Kok-Aral dike traced on the 2025 image, the Muynak range line.
- Narrator: Kokoro `bf_emma`, speeds 0.9–1.0.

## End card

The lock brackets open from the North Aral into a frame on the left: 地图上还写着海 (Noto Serif SC, the map's voice), *The Map Still Says Sea*, a rule, `SATELLITE BRIEFING · 卫星简报`, `LemoLab × Claude Opus 5.5`, over the dimmed Earth turning; a last satellite pass sweeps down behind it. 3.6 s. The "LemoLab × Claude Opus 5.5" sign-off belongs to this library's demo only; a user's film carries no LemoLab credit and no copy of this card.

## Build notes

```

  index.html        two canvases (WebGL2 imagery, 2D marks), fonts
  film.js           render(t): camera keys, plate/scan state, every mark, readouts, subtitles, end card, EV
  engine.js         camera, project/unproject, plate shader (grade, soft scans, growth, printed map, water colour, whip blur)
  overlay.js        hairlines, brackets, readouts, transcript strip, text registry for readcheck
  timeline.js       beats, cues, ring schedule, narration (single source; tools/export.mjs → timeline.json, cues.json, voice/lines.json)
  mix.py            score, foley, beds, voice, mix → out/mix.wav + out/stems/
  tools/            fetch_landsat.py, fetch_gibs.py, plates.py, bmng.py, vectors.py, mapfield.py, growth.py, fonts.py (data); lowcheck.py (sub-bass share);
                    export.mjs, voicefix.py (voice); cuecheck.py, subcheck.mjs, motioncheck.py, audiocheck.py, impactcheck.py, finalasr.py (checks)
  assets/           plates/ (JPEG plates, water masks, mapfield.png, ko_grow.png, plates.json), vectors.json, raw/ (downloads + manifest.jsonl)

```

- `sh demo/build.sh` takes about 2 minutes on Apple silicon (the picture renders in ~20 s with 3 workers). In a fresh clone the plates, raw scenes and fonts are not in git: the first run fetches and rebuilds the imagery (~25 minutes, ~3.5 GB in `assets/raw/`) and downloads the fonts (`tools/fonts.py`: Barlow Condensed and IBM Plex Mono from github.com/google/fonts, Noto SC subsets); `FETCH=1` forces it again. The score needs `sh tools/fetch.sh instruments <lib>` for vsco2ce, vcsl and freepats, the voice `setup.sh deps voice`.
- Checks it runs: `asr_check.py` with `small.en` (the base model hears "sea" as "C"), cue grid, subtitle single-line widths measured with the real fonts (widest line 578 px against 1100 px), `readcheck.mjs`, motion per second (no stretch over 1 s below 0.6 mean pixel change; the slowest second of the film is 1.06), the impact ranking.
- Plates: region mosaics 3917 × 2652 at ~190 m for six years; detail plates at ~32–40 m for the landing, Muynak and Kok-Aral; Blue Marble world (4096 × 2048) and Central Asia. All sampled in one shader pass; memory about 1 GB of textures per render worker.
- Demo-specific pitfalls: the 1977 Landsat 2 mosaic needs nearest-neighbour resampling, dropout-row repair, streak cleaning at 12° on land and one L1GS scene to close a hole in the north-west bay; the 1989 scene of path 161 on 16 August carries a dust plume across the sea and is excluded (`exclude` in `tools/plates_spec.json`); a dike-bounded polder 10–15 km west of Muynak has a straight edge that can read as a seam: it is dimmed while the port is centred and slides out of frame before the range line; the water masks need contour pieces along plate borders removed or a straight line appears in the North Aral; the map's place names other than 咸海 were dropped because a dive gives them less than the reading time they need.

100 BPM, 4/4; every key action on a beat or half-beat (`demo/tools/cuecheck.py`: 0 ms on 26 cues). D minor, turning to D major at the dam.

| Section | Time | Palette | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orbit | 0–1.8 | D drone (pulse bass with 2nd/3rd harmonics), Dm pad, FM telemetry plucks in 8ths, orbit hum, radio hiss, data chatter | lock ping D6 at 0.6, map ping A5 at 1.2 |
| Dive | 1.8–4.95 | plucks to 16ths with the filter opening, hi-hat ticks, noise riser, gran cassa crescendo, rising tone, altitude-counter clicks | everything is sucked out 4.95–5.36 |
| Tear | 5.4 | the map torn away: bass drum, gran cassa, timpani, a fortissimo low-brass stab (trombones, tuba, horns, D minor), crash, a crackling paper rip swept with the scan bar | one of the three heaviest moments |
| Silence 1 | ~5.9–6.6 | thin wind; the tear decays into it | |
| Rewind | 6.6–7.8 | the last 1.8 s of the film's own soundtrack played backwards and speeding up, a reversed tam-tam, counter ticks | the turn into the signature shot |
| Rings | 7.8–13.2 | bass descends D–C–B♭–A–G with the chords Dm–C–B♭–A–Gm (two pad layers); tuba on each root, trombone on the fifth; a sub pulse on every beat, every half beat from 2000; ticks 8ths → 16ths; each ring: timpani on the root + bass drum + inharmonic metal ring + pen hiss; a reversed cymbal swells into a 0.24 s suck-out | acceleration by subdivision, not tempo |
| Stop | 13.2–15.3 | the slam (bass drum, timpani, gran cassa, gong, metal clang), then low D, bowed cymbal, thin drone | the loudest moment of the film |
| Muynak | 15.3–21.9 | distant ship horn (two detuned saws, long room) with a creak, timpani heartbeat every two beats, a low D/A drone whose filter opens with the range line, dry sand grains, ratchet ticks per 2 km (accent every 10 km), a hollow tock + ping when the reading lands | |
| Silence 2 | 21.9–22.8 | wind only | first sound after it: one lap of water at 22.8, before the picture turns north |
| North | 22.8–28.8 | whip crack and swish; a 0.22 s suck-out, then the dam slam (bass drum, timpani, knock, clash, low metal gate); D major: tuba, trombone, horns, a warm pad, bowed vibraphone, a cymbal swell that lands as the water arrives, glass-harp motif D5–A4–C♯5–F♯5–E5–D5 with echoes, vibraphone pulse; water bed | the only wet timbres in the film |
| Climb | 28.8–34.2 | horns D3/A3/F♯4, tuba, bowed vibraphone, D-major pad; the motif on glass and FM ping together (dry and wet united); light pulse | pin ping at 31.2 |
| End | 34.2–37.8 | low D hit, lock-ping echo, a soft sweep for the last pass, long tail | |

Mix (in `mix.py`): stem gains frozen (music 10 dB under the voice while it speaks and ducked about 5 dB, pulse −8 dB, foley −6 dB, beds −17 dB); bus compression on music, pulse, foley and beds only, so the hits keep their weight; a master stage (−14.4 LUFS, true-peak limiter at −4.6 dBTP on 4× oversampled peaks; AAC adds back about 3 dB). Sub-bass: a 38 Hz high-pass (46 Hz, 4th order on hits) and a −5 dB shelf below 62 Hz on everything but the voice; the impacts carry their weight at 60–120 Hz (`punch()`): 20–60 Hz sits 16 dB under the full band, as in the dataviz demo. The film measures −13.8 LUFS, true peak −1.6 dBTP, LRA 5.3 LU. `tools/impactcheck.py`: the hard stop is the loudest momentary moment of the film, the dam slam −0.5 dB and the map tear −2.6 dB under it (each among the loudest 4 s of the film), and they follow dips of −4, −3 and −14 dB. - Plates: region mosaics 3917 × 2652 at ~190 m for six years; detail plates at ~32–40 m for the landing, Muynak and Kok-Aral; Blue Marble world (4096 × 2048) and Central Asia. All sampled in one shader pass; memory about 1 GB of textures per render worker.

fetch_build_specs.text_verbatim:
#!/bin/sh
# One command: 《地图上还写着海》 The Map Still Says Sea (Satellite Briefing demo)
#   sh demo/build.sh            voice, events, picture, score + mix, master, subtitles, checks, poster
#   FETCH=1 sh demo/build.sh    first re-download and rebuild the imagery (Landsat via Planetary Computer,
#                               Blue Marble via NASA GIBS, Natural Earth): ~25 min, ~3.5 GB in assets/raw
# In a fresh clone (plates, raw scenes and fonts are not in git) the imagery and fonts are fetched automatically.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)                 # .../<slug>/demo
FILM=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)                         # .../<slug>
LIB=${LIB:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}            # styles/<slug>/demo -> library root
export LIB
[ -f "$LIB/core/render/video.mjs" ] || { echo "set LIB to the library folder"; exit 1; }
PY="$LIB/.venv/bin/python"
NAME=satellite-briefing
cd "$LIB"

# the test keys on gitignored artefacts: a clean clone has the tracked vectors.json/plates.json but no plates
if [ "${FETCH:-0}" = "1" ] || [ ! -f "$HERE/assets/plates/r2025.jpg" ] || [ ! -f "$HERE/assets/plates/mapfield.png" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$HERE/assets/raw/ne"
  for f in ne_10m_lakes_historic ne_10m_rivers_lake_centerlines; do
    curl -sL -o "$HERE/assets/raw/ne/$f.geojson" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/master/geojson/$f.geojson"
  done
  "$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/fetch_gibs.py" "$HERE"
  for p in r2025 r1977 r1989 r2000 r2009 r2014 la2025 mu2025 ko2001 ko2009 ko2025; do
    "$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/fetch_landsat.py" "$HERE" $p
  done
  "$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/plates.py" "$HERE"
  "$PY" -I "$HERE/tools/bmng.py" "$HERE"

"""Fetch co-registered Landsat plates (public domain, USGS) through the Microsoft
Planetary Computer STAC + data API. The server reprojects each scene to a
lon/lat bbox; we composite the scenes of one year onto one plate grid.

usage: python -I tools/fetch_landsat.py <demo_dir> <plate_name> [--list]
Plates are defined in tools/plates_spec.json. Raw arrays are cached in
assets/raw/landsat/<plate>/<item>.npz; the composite goes to
assets/raw/landsat/<plate>.npz (bands float32 0..1 reflectance-ish + valid mask).
Every request URL is appended to assets/raw/manifest.jsonl.
"""
import json, sys, os, io, math, time, urllib.request, urllib.parse, datetime
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import numpy as np

STAC = 'https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search'
DATA = 'https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/data/v1/item/bbox'
CHUNK = 1400


def http(url, data=None, tries=5, timeout=180):
    for k in range(tries):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'User-Agent': 'lemo-opuscar-film/1.0'})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
                return r.read()
        except Exception as e:
            if k == tries - 1:
                raise
            time.sleep(2 + 3 * k)


def search(spec):
    body = {'collections': [spec['collection']], 'bbox': spec['bbox'], 'datetime': spec['datetime'], 'limit': 250}
    q = {}
    if spec.get('platforms'):
        q['platform'] = {'in': spec['platforms']}
    if q:
        body['query'] = q
    feats = json.loads(http(STAC, json.dumps(body).encode()))['features']
    return feats


def choose(spec, feats):
    """One acquisition date per WRS path (adjacent rows then match), central paths first;
    rows the chosen date misses are filled from the best other date."""
    if spec.get('items'):
        byid = {f['id']: f for f in feats}
        return [byid[i] for i in spec['items'] if i in byid]
    target = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(spec['target'])
    w, s_, e, n = spec['plate']; cx = (w + e) / 2; cy = (s_ + n) / 2
    ok = []
    for f in feats:
        p = f['properties']
        if any(x in f['id'] for x in spec.get('exclude', [])):   # e.g. a scene with a dust plume over the sea
            continue
        if p.get('eo:cloud_cover', 100) > spec.get('max_cloud', 20):
            continue
        if 'L1GS' in f['id'] or 'L1GT' in f['id']:
            continue
        bw, bs, be, bn = f['bbox']
        if be < w or bw > e or bn < s_ or bs > n:
            continue
        ok.append(f)
    def date(f): return f['properties']['datetime'][:10]
    def dd(f): return abs((datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(date(f)) - target).days)
    paths = {}
    for f in ok:
        paths.setdefault(f['properties']['landsat:wrs_path'], []).append(f)
    prim, rest = [], []
    for path, fs in paths.items():
        bydate = {}
        for f in fs:
            bydate.setdefault(date(f), []).append(f)
        best = max(bydate.values(), key=lambda g: (len({x['properties']['landsat:wrs_row'] for x in g}), -sum(x['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover', 0) for x in g) / len(g) * .5 - dd(g[0]) * spec.get('date_w', 1.0)))
        prim += best
        rows = {x['properties']['landsat:wrs_row'] for x in best}
        for f in sorted(fs, key=lambda f: f['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover', 0) * 3 + dd(f) * .25):
            r = f['properties']['landsat:wrs_row']
            if r not in rows:
                rows.add(r); rest.append(f)
    def central(f):
        bw, bs, be, bn = f['bbox']
        return abs((bw + be) / 2 - cx) + .3 * abs((bs + bn) / 2 - cy)
    return sorted(prim, key=central) + sorted(rest, key=central)


def grid(spec):
    w, s, e, n = spec['plate']
    dlon = spec['dlon']
    dlat = dlon * math.cos(math.radians(spec.get('lat0', 45.0)))
    W = int(round((e - w) / dlon)); H = int(round((n - s) / dlat))
    return w, n, dlon, dlat, W, H


def fetch_scene(demo, name, spec, f, log):
    rs = spec.get('resampling', 'bilinear')
    cache = os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/landsat', name + ('' if rs == 'bilinear' else '_' + rs), f['id'] + '.npz')
    if os.path.exists(cache):
        return cache
    w0, n0, dlon, dlat, W, H = grid(spec)
    bw, bs, be, bn = f['bbox']
    x0 = max(0, int(math.floor((bw - w0) / dlon))); x1 = min(W, int(math.ceil((be - w0) / dlon)))
    y0 = max(0, int(math.floor((n0 - bn) / dlat))); y1 = min(H, int(math.ceil((n0 - bs) / dlat)))
    if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0:
        return None
    bands = spec['bands']
    nb = len(bands)
    arr = np.zeros((nb, y1 - y0, x1 - x0), np.uint16)
    msk = np.zeros((y1 - y0, x1 - x0), np.uint8)
    jobs = []
    for cy in range(y0, y1, CHUNK):
        for cx in range(x0, x1, CHUNK):
            cw = min(CHUNK, x1 - cx); ch = min(CHUNK, y1 - cy)
            bb = (w0 + cx * dlon, n0 - (cy + ch) * dlat, w0 + (cx + cw) * dlon, n0 - cy * dlat)
            qs = [('collection', spec['collection']), ('item', f['id'])] + [('assets', b) for b in bands] + [('resampling', rs), ('reproject', rs)]
            url = f"{DATA}/{bb[0]:.6f},{bb[1]:.6f},{bb[2]:.6f},{bb[3]:.6f}/{cw}x{ch}.npy?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(qs)
            jobs.append((cx, cy, cw, ch, url))

    def get(j):
        cx, cy, cw, ch, url = j
        raw = http(url)
        a = np.load(io.BytesIO(raw), allow_pickle=False)
        return j, a

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
        for (cx, cy, cw, ch, url), a in ex.map(get, jobs):
            arr[:, cy - y0:cy - y0 + ch, cx - x0:cx - x0 + cw] = a[:nb]
            msk[cy - y0:cy - y0 + ch, cx - x0:cx - x0 + cw] = (a[nb] > 0)
            log.write(json.dumps({'plate': name, 'item': f['id'], 'url': url, 'accessed': datetime.date.today().isoformat()}) + '\n')
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cache), exist_ok=True)
    np.savez_compressed(cache, arr=arr, msk=msk, x0=x0, y0=y0)
    return cache


def dropouts(arr):
    """thin structures where every MSS band is near zero (scan-line dropouts); wide dark areas (water) are kept"""
    from scipy import ndimage
    low = arr.max(0) < 15
    wide = ndimage.binary_opening(low, structure=np.ones((5, 5)))
    return ndimage.binary_dilation(low & ~wide, iterations=1)


SCAN_DEG = 12.1     # MSS scan lines run at this angle (down-right) on the lon/lat plate grid around the Aral


def destripe(a, off=12, grow=11, thr=0.025):
    """MSS scan-line dropouts: long, thin, straight streaks along the scan direction. Rotate so the scan
    lines are horizontal; a pixel belongs to a streak when it differs from the land 12 px above and below
    it, consistently along 61 px of scan line. Streak pixels are replaced by the average of the land above
    and below; water and coasts are left alone (the shoreline is the measurement)."""
    from scipy import ndimage
    nir = a[-1]
    wet = ndimage.binary_dilation(nir < 0.09, iterations=14)
    for b in range(a.shape[0]):
        x = a[b]
        r = ndimage.rotate(x, SCAN_DEG, reshape=True, order=1, mode='nearest')
        w = ndimage.rotate(wet.astype(np.float32), SCAN_DEG, reshape=True, order=0) > .5
        nb = 0.5 * (np.roll(r, off, 0) + np.roll(r, -off, 0))
        d = r - nb
        dl = ndimage.uniform_filter1d(d, 61, axis=1)
        core = (np.abs(dl) > thr) & ~w
        m = ndimage.binary_dilation(core, structure=np.ones((grow, 1))) & ~w
        fix = np.where(m, nb, r)
        H, W = x.shape
        mb = ndimage.rotate(m.astype(np.float32), -SCAN_DEG, reshape=True, order=1)
        fb = ndimage.rotate(fix, -SCAN_DEG, reshape=True, order=1)
        oy = (mb.shape[0] - H) // 2; ox = (mb.shape[1] - W) // 2
        mb = mb[oy:oy + H, ox:ox + W]; fb = fb[oy:oy + H, ox:ox + W]
        sel = mb > 0.5
        x[sel] = fb[sel]
    return a


def to_refl(spec, arr):
    a = arr.astype(np.float32)
    if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l2':
        return np.clip(a * 2.75e-5 - 0.2, 0, 1)   # USGS C2 L2 surface reflectance scale/offset
    return a / 255.0                               # MSS L1 DN (8-bit) as-is


def main():
    demo, name = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    specs = json.load(open(os.path.join(demo, 'tools/plates_spec.json')))
    spec = specs[name]
    feats = search(spec)
    sel = choose(spec, feats)
    print(f'{name}: {len(feats)} found, {len(sel)} chosen')
    for f in sel:
        p = f['properties']; print('  ', f['id'], p['datetime'][:10], 'cc', p.get('eo:cloud_cover'))
    if '--list' in sys.argv:
        return
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw'), exist_ok=True)
    w0, n0, dlon, dlat, W, H = grid(spec)
    nb = len(spec['bands'])
    comp = np.zeros((nb, H, W), np.float32)
    have = np.zeros((H, W), bool)
    src = np.full((H, W), 255, np.uint8)      # which scene (index into meta.scenes) each pixel came from
    used = []
    from scipy import ndimage
    with open(os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/manifest.jsonl'), 'a') as log:
        for f in sel:
            c = fetch_scene(demo, name, spec, f, log)
            if not c:
                continue
            z = np.load(c, allow_pickle=False)
            x0, y0 = int(z['x0']), int(z['y0'])
            a = to_refl(spec, z['arr']); m = z['msk'].astype(bool)
            m &= (z['arr'][:2] > 0).all(0)          # dropped lines / fill are DN 0 (not low reflectance: water SWIR is ~0)
            if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l1': m &= ~dropouts(z['arr'])   # MSS dropout lines: thin rows with every band near zero
            m = ndimage.binary_erosion(m, iterations=3 if spec.get('resampling') == 'nearest' else 6)   # scene rims: resampling against nodata
            if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l1':
                a = destripe(a, 3, 3, .02) if spec.get('resampling') == 'nearest' else destripe(a)
            h, w = m.shape
            sub = have[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w]
            ov = m & sub
            if ov.sum() > 4000:
                for b in range(nb):
                    r = np.median(comp[b, y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][ov]) / max(1e-4, np.median(a[b][ov]))
                    a[b] *= float(np.clip(r, .75, 1.33))
            put = m & ~sub
            # feather: inside the overlap, blend the new scene in over 40 px from the old coverage's edge
            if ov.any():
                d = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(sub)
                wgt = np.clip(1 - d / 40.0, 0, 1) * ov
                for b in range(nb):
                    cb = comp[b, y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w]
                    cb[ov] = cb[ov] * (1 - wgt[ov]) + a[b][ov] * wgt[ov]
            for b in range(nb):
                comp[b, y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][put] = a[b][put]
            src[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][put] = len(used)
            sub |= put
            used.append({'id': f['id'], 'date': f['properties']['datetime'][:10], 'cloud': f['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover'), 'pixels': int(put.sum())})
    # gap fill: holes left by missing / cloudy rows are filled from a wider window with a looser cloud limit
    if (~have).mean() > 0.002 and spec.get('fill_datetime'):
        fs = dict(spec); fs['datetime'] = spec['fill_datetime']; fs['max_cloud'] = spec.get('fill_cloud', 40)
        cand = [f for f in search(fs) if f['id'] not in {u['id'] for u in used} and 5 <= int(f['properties']['datetime'][5:7]) <= 10 and f['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover', 100) <= fs['max_cloud']]   # summer only; fill may use L1GS (systematic) scenes
        cand.sort(key=lambda f: (('L1GS' in f['id']) * 50 + f['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover', 100)))
        # holes worth filling: inside the plate, away from its rim (the rim may simply lie outside every path)
        rim = 40
        hole = ~have; hole[:rim] = hole[-rim:] = False; hole[:, :rim] = hole[:, -rim:] = False
        tried = 0
        with open(os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/manifest.jsonl'), 'a') as log:
            for f in cand:
                if hole.sum() < 2000 or tried >= spec.get('fill_max', 8):
                    break
                bw, bs, be, bn = f['bbox']
                # the footprint is a rotated square: test only its central 60 %
                cxm, cym = (bw + be) / 2, (bs + bn) / 2; hw, hh = (be - bw) * .3, (bn - bs) * .3
                x0 = max(0, int((cxm - hw - w0) / dlon)); x1 = min(W, int((cxm + hw - w0) / dlon) + 1)
                y0 = max(0, int((n0 - cym - hh) / dlat)); y1 = min(H, int((n0 - cym + hh) / dlat) + 1)
                if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0 or hole[y0:y1, x0:x1].sum() < 2000:
                    continue
                tried += 1
                c = fetch_scene(demo, name, spec, f, log)
                if not c:
                    continue
                z = np.load(c, allow_pickle=False)
                x0, y0 = int(z['x0']), int(z['y0'])
                a = to_refl(spec, z['arr']); m = z['msk'].astype(bool) & (z['arr'][:2] > 0).all(0)
                if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l1': m &= ~dropouts(z['arr'])
                m = ndimage.binary_erosion(m, iterations=14 if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l1' else 6)
                if spec['collection'] == 'landsat-c2-l1':
                    a = destripe(a, 3, 3, .02) if spec.get('resampling') == 'nearest' else destripe(a)
                h, w = m.shape
                sub = have[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w]
                ov = m & sub
                if ov.sum() > 4000:
                    for b in range(nb):
                        r = np.median(comp[b, y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][ov]) / max(1e-4, np.median(a[b][ov]))
                        a[b] *= float(np.clip(r, .75, 1.33))
                put = m & ~sub
                for b in range(nb):
                    comp[b, y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][put] = a[b][put]
                src[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w][put] = len(used)
                sub |= put
                hole[y0:y0 + h, x0:x0 + w] &= ~put
                used.append({'id': f['id'], 'date': f['properties']['datetime'][:10], 'cloud': f['properties'].get('eo:cloud_cover'), 'pixels': int(put.sum()), 'fill': True})
    # thin holes (scan-line dropouts the overlapping scenes did not cover): fill from the neighbours
    gap = ~have & (ndimage.distance_transform_edt(~have) <= 5)
    if gap.any():
        wv = ndimage.gaussian_filter(have.astype(np.float32), 2.5)
        for b in range(nb):
            fv = ndimage.gaussian_filter(comp[b] * have, 2.5)
            comp[b][gap] = (fv / np.maximum(wv, 1e-6))[gap]
        have |= gap & (wv > 0.05)
    out = os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/landsat', name + '.npz')
    np.savez_compressed(out, bands=comp.astype(np.float16), valid=have, src=src, meta=json.dumps({'name': name, 'bands': spec['bands'], 'plate': spec['plate'], 'dlon': dlon, 'dlat': dlat, 'W': W, 'H': H, 'scenes': used}))
    print(f'wrote {out}  {W}x{H}  coverage {have.mean():.3f}')
    for u in used:
        print('   used', u)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Fetch NASA Blue Marble: Next Generation (public domain) from NASA GIBS WMS,
tiled, and stitch it into one lon/lat (EPSG:4326) image.

usage: python -I tools/fetch_gibs.py <demo_dir>
Writes assets/raw/gibs/world.jpg (whole Earth) and assets/raw/gibs/ca.jpg
(Central Asia). Every request URL goes to assets/raw/manifest.jsonl.
"""
import sys, os, io, json, time, datetime, urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from PIL import Image

WMS = 'https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wms/epsg4326/best/wms.cgi'
LAYER = 'BlueMarble_NextGeneration'
JOBS = {
    # name: (west, south, east, north, width, height)
    'world': (-180, -90, 180, 90, 8192, 4096),
    'ca': (40, 30, 80, 60, 4800, 3600),
}
T = 1024


def get(url):
    for k in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'lemo-opuscar-film/1.0'}), timeout=120) as r:
                return r.read()
        except Exception:
            if k == 4:
                raise
            time.sleep(3 + 3 * k)


def main():
    demo = sys.argv[1]
    out = os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/gibs'); os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    log = open(os.path.join(demo, 'assets/raw/manifest.jsonl'), 'a')
    for name, (w, s, e, n, W, H) in JOBS.items():
        dst = os.path.join(out, name + '.jpg')
        if os.path.exists(dst):
            continue
        img = Image.new('RGB', (W, H))
        dx = (e - w) / W; dy = (n - s) / H
        tiles = [(x, y) for y in range(0, H, T) for x in range(0, W, T)]

        def one(xy):
            x, y = xy
            tw = min(T, W - x); th = min(T, H - y)
            bb = (n - (y + th) * dy, w + x * dx, n - y * dy, w + (x + tw) * dx)   # WMS 1.3.0 EPSG:4326 = lat,lon order
            url = (f'{WMS}?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetMap&VERSION=1.3.0&LAYERS={LAYER}&STYLES=&CRS=EPSG:4326'
                   f'&BBOX={bb[0]:.6f},{bb[1]:.6f},{bb[2]:.6f},{bb[3]:.6f}&WIDTH={tw}&HEIGHT={th}&FORMAT=image/jpeg')
            return xy, url, Image.open(io.BytesIO(get(url))).convert('RGB')

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex:
            for (x, y), url, im in ex.map(one, tiles):
                img.paste(im, (x, y))
                log.write(json.dumps({'plate': 'gibs_' + name, 'url': url, 'accessed': datetime.date.today().isoformat()}) + '\n')
        img.save(dst, quality=93)
        print('wrote', dst, W, H)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

## B. 影像实测（本片自己量的）

### B1. 年轮与"还在水下的部分"

方法：每一年用该年 7–10 月无云的 Landsat 场景拼成一张经纬度栅格（每像素 0.0024° 经度 × 0.0017° 纬度，约 190 m）。水体：TM/ETM+/OLI 用 MNDWI（绿 − 短波红外）与 NDWI 联合阈值，MSS 用绿 − 近红外（0.8–1.1 µm）与近红外暗值；只保留落在 Natural Earth 历史海面内、面积 ≥ 25 km² 的水体，填掉 < 3 km² 的小岛。按纬度修正像元面积后求和。岸线 = 水体掩膜 0.5 等值线（marching squares），简化到约 115 m。百分比 = 实测水面 ÷ 68,000 km²（A1）。代码：`tools/fetch_landsat.py`、`tools/plates.py`、`tools/vectors.py`；结果在 `assets/vectors.json` 与 `assets/plates/plates.json`（含每个像元来自哪一景）。

|---|---|---|---|
| 1977 | Landsat 2 MSS，34 景，1977-07-25 至 09-22（含 6 景同年补洞，其中 1 景 L1GS）；扫描线掉线已修补（见 B4） | 54,403 km² | 80% |
| 1989 | Landsat 4/5 TM，27 景，1989-06-14 至 10-13（排除了 1989-08-16 第 161 轨道：湖面上有一道沙尘羽流，改用 09-17） | 39,860 km² | 59% |
| 2000 | Landsat 7 ETM+，28 景，2000-07-17 至 09-29 | 26,879 km² | 40% |
| 2009 | Landsat 5 TM，27 景，2009-07-14 至 09-16 | 14,366 km² | 21% |
| 2014 | Landsat 8 OLI，28 景，2014-07-03 至 09-16 | 7,061 km² | 10% |
| 2025 | Landsat 8/9 OLI，28 景，2025-08-18 至 08-31 | 5,079 km² | 7% |

与官方数字对照：

- NASA EO 2001（*The Shrinking Aral Sea*，https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/the-shrinking-aral-sea-1396/ ）："In the last 30 years, more than 60 percent of the lake has disappeared." 本片 2000 年实测剩 39.5%，即消失约 60%。一致。
- 世界银行 2008 新闻稿："Between 1960 and 2004, the sea's surface area shrank almost 70 percent." 2004 年落在本片 2000 年（39.5%）与 2009 年（21.1%）之间，约 30%。一致。
- USGS Earthshots："It is now only about 10% of the size it was in 1960." NASA EO 2024（https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/dunes-and-desert-replace-the-aral-sea-152887 ）："…has decreased to approximately 10 percent of its original area." 本片 2014 年 10.4%，2025 年 8 月 7.5%（当年夏末偏枯；官方是约数）。画面最后停在实测的 7%，不写"约 10%"，避免两个数字打架。
- 1977 年读数之前的"100%"是地图上的海（A1），不对应任何一张影像。

### B2. 莫伊纳克旧港到今天的海边：95 km

- 起点：莫伊纳克海岸边的废船区（旧港岸线），59.030°E、43.785°N。
- 终点：2025 年 8 月 Landsat 拼接图上南咸海西湖盆（今天仍在的那片海）距起点最近的水体像元，58.323°E、44.467°N。
- 方法：只在包含西湖盆的连通水体里找最近点，用大圆距离（R = 6371.0088 km）：94.5 km，画面和旁白取 95 km。
- 对照：ESA 2003 年图片说明（https://www.esa.int/ESA_Multimedia/Images/2003/07/Fishing_town_Muynak_is_now_150_km_from_water ）"Now the town is 150 km away from water."——那是 2003 年、量到当时另一处水体，参考点不同，所以本片不用 150 km，只用自己按公开方法实测的数。

### B3. 科卡拉尔大坝的位置

白线沿 2025 年 Landsat 上可见的坝体描出：西北臂 60.750°E 46.120°N → 拐角 60.788°E 46.087°N → 东臂 60.865°E 46.088°N。肉眼可见的坝体约 10 km；画面上的"长 13 km"用的是世界银行的数字（A6），不是这条白线的长度。

### B4. 影像修补（不改变测量）

- 1977 年 Landsat 2 MSS 的扫描线掉线（整行近零）按无效像元处理，由相邻场景补；残留的细条纹（约 12° 方向的长直线、请求分块之间的 1 像素接缝）只在陆地上用跨线中值替换，湖面与岸线不动（岸线就是测量对象）。
- 1989 年换掉一景带沙尘羽流的场景，同年 09-17 的同一轨道代替。
- 面积按修补后的影像重新测了一遍（上表）：1977 年比修补前少 0.3%，1989 年因换景少 1.0%，两年的画面读数（80%、59%）都没有变。

## C. 终渲前对照

终渲前逐句核对了 `timeline.js` 里的 10 句旁白与中英字幕、`film.js` 里的全部画面文字，以及 `cues.json`、`satellite-briefing.srt`：每个数字、年份都能在上表找到出处；没有表外的数字。
